mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using the linearity property of Fourier transforms, if } F\{e^{-x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2} \text{ and } F\{e^{-2x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{2}{4+s^2}, \text{ then } F\{3e^{-x} - 2e^{-2x}\} \text{ is:}\)
\(\text{Given } F\{f(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \frac{2i(\sin(as) - as\cos(as))}{s^2}, \text{ what is } F\{f(2x)\} \text{ using the change of scale property?}\)

\(\text{Find the Fourier transform of } f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & |x| \leq 1 \\ 0, & |x| > 1 \end{cases} \text{ given that the transform of } g(x) = \begin{cases} x, & |x| \leq a \\ 0, & |x| > a \end{cases} \text{ is } \frac{2i}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left( \frac{\sin(as) - a s \cos(as)}{s^2} \right).\)
\(\text{Using the modulation theorem, if } F\{e^{-|x|}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2}, \text{ then } F\{e^{-|x|} \cos(3x)\} \text{ is:}\)
\(\text{If } F\{f(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \frac{4(\sin s - s \cos s)}{s^3}, \text{ find } F\{x f(x)\} \text{ using the derivative of transform property.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Consider } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & |x| < 1 \\ 0 & |x| > 1 \end{cases}, \text{ its Fourier transform is } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{\sin s}{s}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{By inverse transform at } x=0: f(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Since } \frac{\sin s}{s} \text{ is even: } \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds = 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds = \pi\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin x}{x} dx = \frac{\pi}{2}.\)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using Fourier transform, evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin x}{x} dx.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{We have } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{1+s^2} \text{ for } f(x)=e^{-|x|}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{By inverse transform at } x=0: f(0)=1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2} ds = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+s^2} ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Since integrand is even: } \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+s^2} ds = 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+x^2} dx = \pi\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+x^2} dx = \frac{\pi}{2}.\)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using the Fourier transform of } f(x)=e^{-|x|}, \text{ evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+x^2} dx.\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
\(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f'(x) e^{isx} dx\)(2)
Integrate by parts: let \(u = e^{isx}\), \(dv = f'(x)dx\)(2)
Then \(du = is e^{isx} dx\), \(v = f(x)\)(2)
\(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left[ f(x)e^{isx} \right]_{-\infty}^{\infty} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) is e^{isx} dx\)(3)
Since \(f(x) \to 0\) as \(x \to \pm\infty\), the boundary term vanishes(2)
\(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = -is \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) e^{isx} dx = -is F(s)\)(4)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find the Fourier transform of the derivative } f'(x) \text{ given that } \mathcal{F}\{f(x)\}=F(s).\)
